bug_semantics: With OAuth enabled behind a reverse proxy that terminates browser-facing HTTPS and forwards to Temporal UI Server over HTTP, authentication cookies used c.Request().TLS != nil to choose Secure. Because that request describes only the proxy-to-server hop, the server emitted the user* access/ID-token cookies and, later, refresh-token cookies without Secure even though the browser authenticated over HTTPS. Exploitation additionally requires steering the UI hostname to attacker-served HTTP, preventing HTTPS, and receiving a later same-site plaintext request while the credential is live; a malicious page alone or passive observation of the successful TLS session is insufficient.
flaw_origin: temporalio/ui-server PR #219 moved the OAuth user session into browser cookies. Its sole source commit 8bca548c78fcadc737626bea96ef1e16075792d6 introduced the sensitive user* cookie and set Secure from c.Request().TLS. GitHub squash commit 821cf598371353f1b579dfe1e87aeb3638b041d6 landed the identical tree and patch. The code was later imported into temporalio/ui, and the 2026 refresh-token work extended the same incorrect transport inference to a longer-lived HttpOnly refresh cookie; those moves and extensions are not the first BIC.
ai_marker: BIC commit-object check: `git cat-file commit 8bca548c78fcadc737626bea96ef1e16075792d6` shows author and committer `feedmeapples <aksenov.ro@outlook.com>` and the message `Store user session in browser`, with no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI, bot, or other automation trailer/identity.
evidence: Vulnerability mechanism: `git show v2.53.1:server/auth/auth.go` in temporalio/ui-server shows SetUser serializing OAuth AccessToken/IDToken into user* cookies with `Secure: c.Request().TLS != nil`; the same function stores an issued refresh token in the `refresh` cookie with that expression. `git show v2.53.1:server/route/auth.go` shows these cookies are issued during the OAuth callback/refresh flow. This exactly matches GHSA-c7mm-29xf-mmqp's reverse-proxy TLS-termination scenario and attack prerequisites.

Squash decomposition: fetch public `refs/pull/219/head` from temporalio/ui-server and run `git log --reverse fca4a6967d9e4fb1c8b1521e185bd70d99ba26d8..refs/pull/219/head`; it contains exactly 8bca548c78fcadc737626bea96ef1e16075792d6. `git cat-file commit 8bca548c78fcadc737626bea96ef1e16075792d6` reports tree 12b0727fd89f1703a5bf20a052cb7a28bb888608 and parent fca4a6967d9e4fb1c8b1521e185bd70d99ba26d8; landed squash 821cf598371353f1b579dfe1e87aeb3638b041d6 has the same tree and parent. Stable patch-id for each is 777cd692b449860d5887c5ebce565c00b99d8396, so the one-member PR head is the smallest reconstructable BIC rather than the squash object.

BIC cross-check: after fetching PR #219, `git log -L 72,82:server/auth/auth.go refs/pull/219/head` attributes creation of the user* cookie, including `Secure: c.Request().TLS != nil`, to 8bca548c78fcadc737626bea96ef1e16075792d6. `git log --all -S'Secure:   c.Request().TLS != nil' -- server/auth/auth.go` finds both that direct member and its identical landed squash, followed only by later sync/removal events.

Direct parent verification: `git show fca4a6967d9e4fb1c8b1521e185bd70d99ba26d8:server/auth/auth.go` has the prior server-side session implementation; its sensitive auth session options explicitly use `Secure: true` and it has no user* cookie whose Secure flag derives from Request().TLS. The BIC diff creates the vulnerable browser-cookie block, establishing parent absence.

Lifecycle: temporalio/ui commit c6f84170173eb9e9d82a98fd78faf4adc8af09ed imported ui-server and is therefore a move, not the BIC. temporalio/ui commits 68f189879f8dbbff00383c004f5547cfbaddbb35 (later reverted) and c67cc8816f0679b1612649facb9796ab506d6e95 (reapplied), synced to ui-server by 7b9ff533fb51beba75497c0a192c66775c08f279, added the refresh cookie with the same faulty Secure derivation; this widened credential lifetime but did not originate the access-token flaw.

Version boundary: in temporalio/ui-server, `git tag --contains 821cf598371353f1b579dfe1e87aeb3638b041d6 --sort=version:refname` starts at v2.7.0; v2.6.2 resolves to 625066db934ad3fabd2e943eca4bbf19266ae883 and its auth.go still uses unconditional `Secure: true`. v2.53.1 resolves to a823c54e83bd348fd9cc76f553ca1582195edab6 and contains the vulnerable access/refresh cookie assignments. Thus the history-supported affected release interval is v2.7.0 through v2.53.1.

Closing fix: temporalio/ui commit 1ed83780edfe2e395048d354976f6487b206b9db (`fix(auth): derive auth cookie Secure attribute from the OIDC callback URL (#3806)`) is the direct source fix: its diff replaces every auth-cookie Request().TLS check with a `secure` value derived once from the configured browser-facing OIDC callback URL scheme. temporalio/ui-server sync commit 8876b80b63003688ab736f45ef28885695a4f6db carries those auth.go/route/auth.go changes into the released server. `git tag --contains 8876b80b63003688ab736f45ef28885695a4f6db --sort=version:refname` starts at v2.53.2 (then v2.53.3); v2.53.2 resolves to 9e46482f9fca17fa9d5979e5459b96741ae4b2b5. The temporalio/ui tag containment for direct fix 1ed83780edfe2e395048d354976f6487b206b9db likewise starts at v2.53.2.

BIC-only AI evidence: the raw 8bca548c78fcadc737626bea96ef1e16075792d6 commit object contains only a human author/committer and its one-line subject, with no AI/automation marker. The GitHub squash object's different GitHub committer and PR-number subject were not used for AI attribution, nor were PR-body or later/fix signals.
reasoning: The vulnerable security decision first appears when PR #219 changes the session architecture from server-side cookies fixed Secure=true to client-side token-bearing cookies whose Secure flag reflects the backend request's TLS state. The public PR head decomposes the squash to one exact member with the same parent, tree, and patch, so 8bca548c78fcadc737626bea96ef1e16075792d6 is the smallest real BIC. Its immediate parent directly lacks the faulty derivation. Later repository import, refresh-token additions, reverts/reapplications, and ui-server sync commits preserve or extend the mechanism but are not origin commits. The source fix 1ed83780edfe2e395048d354976f6487b206b9db uses the browser-facing callback URL, and released sync 8876b80b63003688ab736f45ef28885695a4f6db closes the v2.53.1/v2.53.2 boundary. The BIC object has no AI marker and identifies a human author/committer, so the only evidence-permitted closed verdict is NOT_AI.
